newsitem.title: USA: Quaker sees better margins in some markets.
newsitem.headline: Quaker sees better margins in some markets.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co Chairman William Smithburg said he sees good potential for significant margin improvements in Snapple beverages, Gatorade sports drink in Europe and Latin America, and its food service business.

In the text of a speech given at a Prudential Securities conference, Smithburg said Quaker expects "excellent profit and controllable earnings improvements" in 1996 for many key businesses, including Gatorade, hot cereals, Golden Grain, food service and international foods.
But he reiterated that Snapple, which accounts for about 10 percent of the company's sales, has not delivered the growth or profitability that was originally anticipated.
Quaker bought Snapple nearly two years ago in a $1.7 billion deal.

Smithburg said a new advertising and sampling campaign for Snapple, launched in late-July, came too late to reap any financial benefits for the current beverage season. "But we pursued this program to give us the opportunity to understand what levers move the business at the consumer level, so we can build our tactical plans for next year," he said.

"And while our strategic plans are in process, we are putting a 'floor' under Snapple to limit the financial risk it will add to our 1997 earnings," Smithburg added. "Once through this year of aggressive spending, the business can be run profitability for the future."

Gatorade has close to 10 percent sales growth in the United States and excellent operating margin improvement, Smithburg said. "Results to date are in line with Gatorade's nine percent compound average annual growth rate in the U.S."

Gatorade generates more than $300 million of its annual sales from its international business, focused on Latin America and the Asia Pacific region. In 1995, Gatorade's total worldwide sales were about $1.3 billion.

In Europe, where marketing was cut back in Italy and the Mediterranean area, Gatorade is on track to be break-even in 1996 and earn profits growing forward. Latin America is modestly profitable now, with expanded margins expected, he said.
In hot cereals, Smithburg said Quaker is introducing a new product aimed at consumers over 40, Quaker Quick'n Hearthy, and two new flavors of oatmeal for children.

In ready-to-eat cereals, he said recently price cuts have hurt operating margins. "But, given that we have not changed the promotional activities we had already sold in to the trade, our recent market shares remain strong," Smithburg said.

In food service, margins are improving in Quaker's coffee business, which suffered last year due to rising coffee bean prices. Smithburg said products made for McDonald's Corp restaurants and Quaker food service products are doing well.
"...(W)e expect continued margin recovery as we move forward," he said.
